text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak in Harare calls for constructive dialogue to increase economic ties between the Group of 15 and the Group of 7 industrial nations; demands increasing exports of the southern countries and easing the transfer of technology to them. Mubarak says he is deeply concerned at the fighting in Zaire and calls for it to end immediately.
- The president at the second closed session of Harare meetings: wonder and suprise at the protectionist measures of the advanced countries.
- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri says will take decisive measures after tallying the number of illegally constructed buildings. State to rent rather than sell its flats.
- Rescue operations in the collapsed Heliopolis building are over. Local council to demolish illegal 13-storey building in Medinet Nasr.
- Cairo stock exchange turnover is one billion pounds in October.

- Mubarak says: developing countries need the most cooperation and corelation. Economic development in Egypt is progressing and investment had become more attractive. Final communique will ask for the Group of 15 to be incorporated in the world economic system.
- Mubarak in Damascus today to discuss the peace process.
- Ganzouri says that the system whereby tenants owned their flats has led to carelessness and lack of maintenance.
- Israeli businessmen: Israel's economy is paying the price of Prime Minister Netanyahu's policies.

- Mubarak speaks on behalf of Africa at the Group of 15 conference in Harare. Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe says: We support a second term for U.N. secretary general Boutrous Ghali and refuse the hegemony of the big powers.
- Interior Minister Hassan al-Alfi says Egypt is ready to secure the economic conference.
